Now I can see the issue clearly. Looking at the test case on line 26: `dot.delete(obj, 'cool.hello.0');` - this is trying to delete the first element (index 0) from the array `obj.cool.hello`. 

The bug is that when `obj` is an array at line 68, the code uses `obj.splice(path, 1)` instead of `obj.splice(attr, 1)`. The `path` variable contains the full path string (like "cool.hello.0") while `attr` contains just the last segment ("0"). 

This means when trying to delete from an array, it's trying to use the full path string as the array index, which will fail or behave unexpectedly.
